description: DONS is a discrete-event network simulator with a data-oriented, multi-threaded engine that parallelises a simulation automatically within one server, presented at ACM SIGCOMM 2023 as fast and affordable discrete-event network simulation. Built on the Unity game engine's data-oriented technology stack (DOTS), it achieves high core utilisation, low cache misses and memory efficiency, and shows link congestion and flow completion times in real time; the sample task simulates traffic on the Abilene research backbone, and topology and traffic demands can be changed. Coverage: generic networks, notably data-centre and wide-area topologies. Format and access: source code on GitHub, archived on Zenodo as version 0.1.0 in August 2023; it runs in the Unity Editor 2021.3 with preview DOTS packages; free, with the licence terms in the repository. Caveats: depends on a specific Unity version and preview packages; a research prototype. Simulation uses: large-scale network flow and capacity studies, such as congestion in data-centre networks, where packet-level simulators like ns-3 are slow. Related records: ns-3 and OMNeT++ are general network simulators.
